It had been a long day. Jesus had just fed more than five thousand people with five loaves and two fish.
Then He sent His disciples ahead across the Sea of Galilee, and went up a mountain alone to pray.
Night fell. Out on the lake, the wind turned against them.
For hours they pulled at the oars, and the waves kept pounding the boat.
Then, a little before dawn, they saw something moving toward them across the water.
A man. Walking on the waves.
But a familiar voice called out: “Take courage. It is I. Don’t be afraid.”
Peter shouted back, “Lord, if it’s You, tell me to come to You on the water.” Jesus said one word: “Come.”
Peter climbed over the side, and stepped onto the sea — and walked.
But when he looked at the wind and the waves, he panicked and began to sink. “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and caught him. “Why did you doubt?”
They climbed into the boat — and the wind stopped.
And the disciples fell down and worshiped Him, saying: “Truly, You are the Son of God.”
